questions.question: For RM(r,m), what is the codeword length n?
options: n = 2^m
n = m^2
n = 2^r
n = r + m
questions.explanation: A Reed-Muller codeword lists the polynomial’s output on every input x ∈ {0,1}^m, so there are 2^m positions.

questions.question: What does a generator matrix G do for a linear code?
options: Maps message bits to codewords by linear combination of rows (over the code’s field)
Computes the Hamming distance between two codewords
Finds the minimum distance d directly from a single codeword
Encrypts a message using a secret key
questions.explanation: In a linear code, every codeword is a linear combination of generator rows; encoding is message · G (mod the field).

questions.question: For RM(r,m), what is the dimension k (number of message bits) in terms of binomial coefficients?
options: k = sum_{i=0..r} C(m,i)
k = C(r,m)
k = m + r
questions.explanation: There is one coefficient per monomial of degree ≤ r, and there are C(m,i) monomials of degree i.

questions.question: In the monomial-truth-table view, what is a row of the RM(r,m) generator matrix?
options: The monomial’s value evaluated on all points x = 0..2^m-1
A random binary vector chosen for good distance
The received word after channel noise
The parity-check equations written as columns
questions.explanation: Each monomial defines a Boolean function; evaluating it on every input gives a length-n basis codeword (a generator row).

questions.question: What special class of functions does RM(1,m) represent?
options: Affine functions f(x) = a0 + sum_i ai x_i (mod 2)
All Boolean functions on m variables
Only constant functions
Only quadratic polynomials
questions.explanation: Degree ≤ 1 means “constant + linear terms”, which is exactly an affine Boolean function.

questions.question: In Walsh-Hadamard decoding for RM(1,m), what does the index of the maximum-magnitude transform coefficient identify?
options: The linear coefficient vector (a1..am) of the decoded affine function
The number of errors that occurred in the channel
The parity-check matrix for RM(1,m)
The constant term a0 directly, without any sign information
questions.explanation: The transform computes correlations with all linear functions; the best-matching linear term vector is the argmax index.

questions.question: For RM(1,m), the minimum distance is d = 2^(m-1). What is the unique hard-decision correction radius t?
options: t = m - 1
questions.explanation: Unique correction radius is floor((d-1)/2); with d = 2^(m-1), this is 2^(m-2) - 1.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to always return a decoded RM(1,m) message even when the error rate is beyond the correction radius?
options: Because the decoder can miscorrect and silently output the wrong message
Because RM(1,m) codewords are not linear
Because Walsh-Hadamard transforms require floating point
Because it makes the code rate larger than 1
questions.explanation: Beyond the unique decoding radius, multiple codewords may be similarly close; choosing one can produce undetected corruption unless you add an outer integrity check.
